name: cards-stack

capacity.note: past four rows the stack overflows

density.note: a stacked card is a short paragraph at most

description: Parallel items stacked vertically, full-width cards.
purpose: Use when the items want vertical reading order — sequential exploration rather than a-glance comparison. 2–4 items work best (a fourth fits with the `compact` modifier).

cards.description: Each list item becomes one stacked card. Authoring contract: a top-level bullet is the card title (renders bold by default); an indented bullet underneath carries the body text. An optional trailing inline `code` on the title line renders as a right-anchored pill.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: cards-stack -->

## Slide heading.

- First card title
  - Body text for the first stacked card, two short sentences max.
- Second card title
  - Body text for the second stacked card.
- Third card title
  - Body text for the third stacked card.
sample:
<!-- _class: cards-stack -->

## The stack ranks three cards top to bottom.

- Order is the argument.
  - The stack reads as priority; the top card wins.
- Three is the sweet spot.
  - Bodies run a short paragraph at most.
- Sixteen words per card.
  - The budget that keeps rows breathing.

stressDoc.summary: Four rows with pills — the limit.
stressDoc.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-stack compact -->

## Four rows with pills is the stack's ceiling.

- Row one `shipped`
  - A body at the hard budget holds two sentences; the pill carries the status so the prose does not have to.
- Row two `on track`
  - compact is doing quiet work here — without it, four bodies this size would crowd the footer before the last row lands.
- Row three `at risk`
  - Keep the densest row third; the eye expects trouble near the bottom and reads it with full attention.
- Row four `blocked`
  - The hard stop. A fifth row overflows; split the stack or drop to list-tabular.

whenToUse.title: Vertical reading order
whenToUse.body: The audience scans top-to-bottom, not grid-style. Use when each card builds on the previous one as the eye moves down the slide.

whenToUse.title: Two sentences per card
whenToUse.body: More body than cards-grid can hold without crowding. cards-stack lets each card carry one or two short sentences without losing the layout balance.

whenToUse.title: Two or three items
whenToUse.body: Sweet spot is three. Past that the slide overflows — split across multiple slides or switch to cards-grid with shorter body text per card.

antiPatterns.title: Five or more items
antiPatterns.body: A fourth card fits with the `compact` modifier; past four the stack overflows. For five or more parallel items reach for cards-grid four, or split across slides.

antiPatterns.title: One-line cards
antiPatterns.body: If each card is a single short phrase, the stack reads as a padded list. Drop to `list` (or its `takeaway` variant) and reclaim the vertical space.

antiPatterns.title: Forced sequence
antiPatterns.body: Cards-stack is parallel content read in vertical order, not a numbered sequence. For explicit steps, use list-steps or list-criteria.

related.name: cards-grid
related.when: three or four parallel items in a scannable grid

related.name: compare-prose
related.when: exactly two items, side by side

related.name: list-steps
related.when: items carry an explicit, ordered sequence

horizontal.label: Horizontal cards
horizontal.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-stack horizontal -->

## horizontal lays the stack on its side.

- Rows become columns.
  - The ranking now reads left to right.
- Same card anatomy.
  - Title, body, optional status pill.
- Use for timelines.
  - Sequence feels natural sideways.

numbered.label: Numbered stack
numbered.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-stack -->

## An ordered list makes the ranking explicit.

1. Numbers stamp the rank
   - The stack's order stops being implicit.
2. Three still rules
   - Numbering does not raise the ceiling.
3. Parallel or nothing
   - Ranked cards must match shapes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a `numbered` class to the slide, expecting it to turn on corner numbers.
commonMistakes.fix: There is no `numbered` CSS class — the ranking numbers come purely from authoring the cards as an ordered list (`1.`) instead of `-`.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a fourth card without the `compact` modifier.
commonMistakes.fix: A fourth card only fits with `compact` — without it, four full-size stacked cards overflow the frame; the component's own stress sample demonstrates `cards-stack compact` at four rows.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: Vertical, top-to-bottom priority reading — the base look.
The sequence reads more naturally left-to-right, e.g. a timeline — pivots the stack onto its side.
The vertical rank should be explicit rather than implied by position — author as an ordered list to stamp corner numbers.
